name: Leadpages
summary: Landing pages, pop-ups and alert bars, with unlimited traffic on every Leadpages plan where metered rivals count visitors. The value pick rather than the optimisation pick.
best_for: small businesses building landing pages and simple funnels who want unmetered traffic: no per-visitor anxiety, unlike metered rivals
skip_if: you need deep A/B experimentation or enterprise features: multivariate testing and Smart Traffic start at Optimize ($199/mo) and auto-optimisation on Enterprise
honest_knock: It's the value pick, not the optimisation pick, if you're spending big on ads, Unbounce's Smart Traffic and Instapage's 1:1 personalisation go deeper.

pricing.entry_price_terms: per month ($23 billed annually), 25 pages, 1 site
pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-10-15 against Leadpages' own machine-readable pricing file at leadpages.com/pricing.md, dated 2026-10-10, and the pricing page in a live browser; USD) The Starter plan is gone, so the cheapest plan is now Pro. Five paid plans plus Enterprise and a 7-day free trial that requires a credit card and converts unless you cancel. Publishing plans: Pro $29/mo or $23 billed annually ($276 a year), 25 pages, 1 site, 1 blog, 5 active integrations and API access; Business $49/mo or $39 annually ($468), 50 pages, 2 sites and lead export. Neither includes A/B testing. Testing and optimisation plans: Grow $99/mo or $79 annually ($948), unlimited pages, 4 sites, manual two-way A/B testing, dynamic text replacement, lead enrichment and anonymous traffic detection; Optimize $199/mo or $159 annually ($1,908), 6 sites, 3 seats, up to four variants, Smart Traffic, heatmaps and auto-personalisation; Enterprise is set up with sales (Scale from $399/mo in the USD reference, or $319 a month billed annually at $3,828) and includes 10 sites, 10 seats, auto-optimisation, cross-page learning, role-based access and audit logs. Annual billing is 20% off. No plan has a traffic cap. Add-ons: $20 a month per extra seat or extra custom domain, $40 per extra client workspace on Scale, and AI credit top-ups from $2.50 for 2,000 credits down to $0.60 per thousand at the 150,000-credit pack. For buyers outside the US: read from a European connection on 15 October 2026, the pricing page shows euros, with Pro at €29 and Business at €49 but Grow at €115 and Optimize at €229 a month, against $99 and $199. That page shows Pro, Business, Grow and Optimize as plan cards and names Scale only in its FAQ. Re-read on 15 November 2026 by plain fetch: leadpages.com/pricing.md, now dated 2026-11-12, lists the same five plans at the same monthly and annual prices, the same add-ons and the same AI credit packs. Three things changed. The file now answers "Is there a free plan?" with yes; leadpages.com/llms.txt explains that a free account can build and preview pages, but going live, custom slugs and search-engine indexing need a paid plan or an active trial. The trial checkout can show a trial fee: the file names $1 and the pricing page €1, which counts toward the first month. The public pricing card calls the top tier Enterprise. The USD reference labels it Scale (sold as Enterprise, from $399/mo).

recent_change.text: Leadpages now splits an account into organizations and workspaces. The organization holds the plan, billing and team seats, while workspaces separate work by client, brand or project without separate billing. There are four roles (Owner, Admin, Member, Viewer), invites go out by email or a shareable link, pages can move between workspaces, and an audit log lists recent actions. Viewer and the audit log are Scale-plan features.

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 19 November 2026 the session tested Leadpages in the 7-day Business trial that we started through Paddle. Piper built a draft landing page from one prompt in 61.4 seconds for 850 credits. The plans have changed: Business at EUR 49 replaces Pro, and the pricing page lists unlimited traffic only from Grow. Cancelling took 4 steps with a 50% offer whose exit is a text link. Account and start: we created the account and started the 7-day Business trial through Paddle with his own card. Our AI assistant ran the test in its own tab on 19 November 2026 from 17:25 CET. The interface was in English; the left sidebar with the account name was cropped from the screenshots. Billing at the start: Business EUR 49 a month, Trial ends November 26, 2026. The AI credits read 10,000 while the same page says Includes 20,000 trial credits, so the page contradicts itself. Plans on the billing page, monthly: Business EUR 49 (50 pages, 2 custom domains, MCP connector, 20,000 AI credits a month), Grow EUR 115 (Unlimited pages, 5 active integrations), Optimize EUR 229 (A/B testing with Smart Traffic) and Scale EUR 399; annual saves 20%. Extra credits cost from $2.50 for 2,000 to $90 for 150,000; none bought. Core action, a landing page from a prompt: Create a page opened Piper, the page assistant. One prompt for a made-up local plumber with a hero, three benefits and a quote request form. Piper asked What should I use for images? (we skipped images) and offered three styles. The page was ready in about 2 minutes including 3 choice clicks: Built your page in 61.4s, 850 credits, with 7 sections and a quote form, as Draft, not published. Credits went from 10,000 to 9,150. The footer said 2024, a year the AI set itself. A template, Fitness Gym, copied unchanged in about 30 seconds and used 122 credits. Pages showed Business 2 / 50 pages. Form and leads: the form settings have a redirect URL, UTM capture, a CAPTCHA, appointment booking and No integrations connected to this form. Leads showed Form submissions 0; the rows shown are demo fill. A pop-up from one prompt became a draft, Free Quote Checklist Offer, with no extra credits seen. Analytics showed CONVERSIONS 0 and SESSIONS 0. Connectors list 26 apps, 2 connected by default; nothing else was connected. The MCP Server page lets AI agents create and manage pages; nothing was connected. Paddle portal: This subscription is currently trialing. This trial will end on Nov 26, 2026 after which you will be charged EUR 49.00 a month, which is EUR 40.50 plus 21% tax of EUR 8.50. First payment of Business EUR 0.00, Paid, on Nov 19, 2026. Checkout: the trial checkout was done by us before the session and was not seen. Cancelling, done the same day: Billing, Danger Zone, Cancel Subscription, with the warning Canceling your subscription will revert your account to the Free plan at the end of your billing period. Your pages will expire after 7 days. Step 1, What made you cancel?, five reasons with no option for just testing; we chose Not using it enough. Step 2, what worked well: Easy to build and publish. Step 3, Limited offer: How about 50% off your subscription for 3 months?, EUR 24.50 a month, with Take offer as the main button and Cancel subscription as a text link. Step 4, We will miss you, an optional feedback box and Confirm cancellation. After a reload Billing showed Subscription canceled with Reactivate Subscription. No password and no support contact. Not tested: publishing, a custom domain, A/B tests, traffic limits, connecting apps, buying credits, upgrading and seats. Clean up: two draft pages and one draft pop-up stay; the subscription is cancelled. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The billing page shows 10,000 credits and says it includes 20,000. The AI set the footer year to 2024. In the cancel flow the exit is a plain text link next to a Take offer button, and there is no just testing reason.

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 19 November 2026 the session tested Leadpages in the 7-day Business trial that we started through Paddle. Piper built a draft landing page from one prompt in 61.4 seconds for 850 credits. The plans have changed: Business at EUR 49 replaces Pro, and the pricing page lists unlimited traffic only from Grow. Cancelling took 4 steps with a 50% offer whose exit is a text link. Account and start: we created the account and started the 7-day Business trial through Paddle with his own card. Our AI assistant ran the test in its own tab on 19 November 2026 from 17:25 CET. The interface was in English; the left sidebar with the account name was cropped from the screenshots. Billing at the start: Business EUR 49 a month, Trial ends November 26, 2026. The AI credits read 10,000 while the same page says Includes 20,000 trial credits, so the page contradicts itself. Plans on the billing page, monthly: Business EUR 49 (50 pages, 2 custom domains, MCP connector, 20,000 AI credits a month), Grow EUR 115 (Unlimited pages, 5 active integrations), Optimize EUR 229 (A/B testing with Smart Traffic) and Scale EUR 399; annual saves 20%. Extra credits cost from $2.50 for 2,000 to $90 for 150,000; none bought. Core action, a landing page from a prompt: Create a page opened Piper, the page assistant. One prompt for a made-up local plumber with a hero, three benefits and a quote request form. Piper asked What should I use for images? (we skipped images) and offered three styles. The page was ready in about 2 minutes including 3 choice clicks: Built your page in 61.4s, 850 credits, with 7 sections and a quote form, as Draft, not published. Credits went from 10,000 to 9,150. The footer said 2024, a year the AI set itself. A template, Fitness Gym, copied unchanged in about 30 seconds and used 122 credits. Pages showed Business 2 / 50 pages. Form and leads: the form settings have a redirect URL, UTM capture, a CAPTCHA, appointment booking and No integrations connected to this form. Leads showed Form submissions 0; the rows shown are demo fill. A pop-up from one prompt became a draft, Free Quote Checklist Offer, with no extra credits seen. Analytics showed CONVERSIONS 0 and SESSIONS 0. Connectors list 26 apps, 2 connected by default; nothing else was connected. The MCP Server page lets AI agents create and manage pages; nothing was connected. Paddle portal: This subscription is currently trialing. This trial will end on Nov 26, 2026 after which you will be charged EUR 49.00 a month, which is EUR 40.50 plus 21% tax of EUR 8.50. First payment of Business EUR 0.00, Paid, on Nov 19, 2026. Checkout: the trial checkout was done by us before the session and was not seen. Cancelling, done the same day: Billing, Danger Zone, Cancel Subscription, with the warning Canceling your subscription will revert your account to the Free plan at the end of your billing period. Your pages will expire after 7 days. Step 1, What made you cancel?, five reasons with no option for just testing; we chose Not using it enough. Step 2, what worked well: Easy to build and publish. Step 3, Limited offer: How about 50% off your subscription for 3 months?, EUR 24.50 a month, with Take offer as the main button and Cancel subscription as a text link. Step 4, We will miss you, an optional feedback box and Confirm cancellation. After a reload Billing showed Subscription canceled with Reactivate Subscription. No password and no support contact. Not tested: publishing, a custom domain, A/B tests, traffic limits, connecting apps, buying credits, upgrading and seats. Clean up: two draft pages and one draft pop-up stay; the subscription is cancelled. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The billing page shows 10,000 credits and says it includes 20,000. The AI set the footer year to 2024. In the cancel flow the exit is a plain text link next to a Take offer button, and there is no just testing reason.

friction.export_route: No export or reimport was performed; no file was downloaded or examined. The two categorised kit records were not entered; the objects tested were not kit records.
